Co-plaintiff/applicant/intervener: Heinrich von Bobenhausen, administrator of the Grand Mastership in Prussia and master of the German and non-German lands of the Teutonic Order
Co-defendant/intervener: Mayor and council of the imperial city of Rothenburg ob der Tauber
Procurator for the plaintiff: Dr. Laurentius Vomelius Stapert (1575)
Procurators for the defendant: Dr. Julius Mart (1564); Dr. Christoph Reiffsteck (1581); Dr. Georg Kirwang (1587); Dr. Georg Melchior Kirwang (1589); Dr. Christodorus Engelhardt (1593)
Subject of the case (contemporary): primum mandatum concerning distraint, several seized dogs and other matters (also concerning hunting in Rothenburg's territorial boundary)
Subject of the case (modern): dispute over hunting rights;
When Leonhard Schreck was hunting hares on a stubble field before the Klingentor in early October 1577, Leonhard Scheiblein, Rothenburg's inner master builder, seized eleven dogs and the spear from him with five riders. He also had to promise under oath to appear when summoned.
The plaintiff, the German master, claims for the commander at Rothenburg the right to hunt within the imperial city's territorial boundary. The defendant first responds that Schreck had come to the Teutonic House with the headman Philipp Neidlinger of Ickelheim, but according to Commander Johann von Gleichen did not serve there; moreover, he had let several dogs run into a vineyard, so the seizure served to protect citizens' property from damage. It subsequently declares that it recognizes no hunting right of the commanders within the boundary, since the commandery was originally intended as a parish house, some commanders had served as pastors, and ecclesiastical law prohibited them from hunting in that capacity.
In its judgment of 4 November 1601, the Imperial Chamber Court declared the interference with the plaintiff's hunting right in Rothenburg's territorial boundary improper.
Instances: 1. Imperial Chamber Court, 1578–1602 (1578–1593)
Draft settlement between the plaintiff German master and the mayor and council of the imperial city of Rothenburg, 1577 (Q 7);
Rothenburg commission roll (Q 14) contains: 1581 inspection record of the place of distraint (fol. 63v ff.); privilege of King Maximilian I for the defendant imperial city concerning the territorial boundary, 1507 (fol. 71v ff.); game-ban agreement of Margraves Georg von Brandenburg-Ansbach and Albrecht Alcibiades von Brandenburg-Kulmbach with the defendant imperial city, 1543 (fol. 76r ff.); pleadings and judgment of 1535 in the defendant imperial city's legal dispute with Count Wolfgang von Hohenlohe (see file no. 10979) (fol. 82r ff.); agreement of Count Wolfgang von Hohenlohe with the defendant imperial city concerning game ban and hunting, 1539 (fol. 99v ff.); pleadings and judgment of 1565 in the defendant imperial city's legal dispute with Zaisolph von Rosenberg (fol. 101v ff.); witness statements before an imperial commission, 1581 (fol. 110r ff., 160r ff.);
German-master commission roll (Q 20a) contains: witness statements before an imperial commission, 1582 (fol. 76r ff.); list with sources of expenditure for dogs kept at the Teutonic House in Rothenburg, 1526–1578 (fol. 288v ff.);
Rothenburg commission roll (Q 20b) contains: statement by fiscal advocate Cyriak Ruland, doctor of laws, in 1582 before M. Balthasar Schwind, protonotary at the Imperial Chamber Court, as imperial commissioner
